## Executive summary

First UX cycle for EventPixels. Methods: read-only inspection of public explorer/search/login surfaces and admin edition roster, import wizards, merge/remove confirmations, and shared drawers; compared sibling interaction patterns for the same operator/visitor jobs; cross-checked the Findings Register before minting UX IDs.

Public Event Explorer has inconsistent clear/reset and search feedback; admin edition roster reorder and import create-new gates teach incompatible models across sibling surfaces. Net change: **4 new** Findings (`UX-001`…`UX-004`). **0 resolved**. Strengths: company merge type-to-confirm, remove/discard modals with clear scope copy, Event Explorer fetch-error keep-previous + Retry, mobile filter drawer focus trap, PA create-new acknowledgment (should be the template).

## Findings

### UX-001 — Event Explorer “Clear all” / “Reset Filters” controls disagree

- **Why it matters:** On `/events`, three reset affordances use overlapping language but different semantics. Filter panel header **Clear all** and footer **Reset Filters** both call `resetAll()` (filters **and** sort). Active Filters **Clear all** clears filters only and **keeps sort**. Visitors cannot predict whether “clear” resets sort; same label, different outcomes raises confusion and unnecessary rework on a core public task.
- **Severity:** High · **Effort:** Small
- **Evidence:**
  - `EventExplorerPage.tsx` — `handleReset` → `resetAll()`; `handleClearAllFilters` clears query/topics/regions/dates only
  - `FilterPanelShell.tsx` — header button label **Clear all** → `onReset` (= `handleReset`)
  - `FilterPanel.tsx` — **Reset Filters** → same `onReset` / `resetAll()` (sort included despite “Filters” label)
  - `EventExplorerActiveFilters.tsx` — **Clear all** → `onClearAll` (= `handleClearAllFilters`)
- **Status:** Open
- **Recommended action:** Unify reset semantics and labels (one “clear filters” that never resets sort unless explicitly “reset all including sort”). Make every control with the same label do the same thing.
- **Scope:** Public Events explorer (desktop filter panel, mobile drawer, active-filter chips).
- **Validation / acceptance criteria:** Same-named reset actions produce identical outcomes; labels match what is reset; documented expected behavior in UI copy.
- **Uncertainty / false-positive risk:** Low — code paths are explicit. Intentional dual semantics would still fail the same-label test.
- **Related:** Distinct from `UX-002` (search field feedback).

---

### UX-002 — Events global search clears after submit and desyncs from the applied query

- **Why it matters:** On the Event Explorer page, submitting Global search applies the query via the filter bridge then `clearOnSubmit` empties the field. Empty submit is a deliberate no-op (clear only via chip × or Clear all). The bar no longer shows the active query, so visitors may think search failed or cannot edit/refine without hunting chips — high friction on the primary public find-events path. Sponsor scope syncs query from URL (contrast).
- **Severity:** High · **Effort:** Small
- **Evidence:**
  - `GlobalSearchBar.tsx` — `clearOnSubmit={isEventExplorerPage}`; empty trimmed submit returns early; applied query not bound into the input
  - `SearchBar.tsx` — local input only; no URL/bridge sync when used from Global search on Events
  - `globalSearchBarNavigation.test.ts` — locks clear-on-submit / empty no-op policy
  - Applied text surfaces in `EventExplorerActiveFilters` chips only
  - Contrast: `SponsorSearchCombobox` uses `queryFromUrl` on `/sponsors`
- **Status:** Open
- **Recommended action:** Keep the search field synchronized with the applied Events query (like Sponsors), and/or allow empty submit or an explicit clear control in the bar; do not blank the field after a successful apply without showing the active value elsewhere at equal prominence.
- **Scope:** Marketing Global search on `/events`; Event Explorer bridge.
- **Validation / acceptance criteria:** After search, visitors can see and edit the active query in the primary search control; clearing behavior is discoverable and consistent with Sponsors where applicable.
- **Uncertainty / false-positive risk:** Low on mechanism. Policy may have been intentional to avoid duplicating chips — still fails feedback clarity for the primary control.
- **Related:** `UX-001` (reset labeling); not Product (search exists).

---

### UX-003 — Edition roster reorder uses incompatible save models (sponsors vs exhibitors)

- **Why it matters:** The same admin job — reorder linked companies on an edition — uses draft-then-save with unsaved warnings on **Live sponsors**, but immediate persist on every ↑/↓ for **Exhibitors** (and Partner Alumni member moves). Operators trained on sponsors expect local unsaved order; on exhibitors every click is live with no batch undo — error-prevention and consistency failure on a frequent ops task.
- **Severity:** High · **Effort:** Medium
- **Evidence:**
  - `EditionSponsorsPanel.tsx` — local draft roster; `window.confirm` before discard of unsaved order; save footer via `LiveSponsorOrderSaveBar` / `LiveSponsorOrderSaveFooter`
  - `EditionExhibitorsPanel.tsx` — `handleMove` POSTs `/exhibitors/reorder` immediately; no unsaved bar
  - `SeriesPartnerAlumniPanel.tsx` — member move also immediate (sibling pattern)
- **Status:** Open
- **Recommended action:** Align roster reorder to one interaction model (prefer draft + explicit save + discard confirm for all live edition rosters, or document and apply immediate-persist everywhere with equal undo/feedback). Do not leave sibling tabs teaching opposite save semantics.
- **Scope:** Admin edition Live sponsors / Exhibitors; series Partner Alumni member order (related).
- **Validation / acceptance criteria:** Reorder save/discard semantics match across edition roster surfaces; operators get equivalent unsaved or undo affordances.
- **Uncertainty / false-positive risk:** Low on inconsistency. Immediate persist can be a deliberate trade-off for exhibitors — still fails cross-tab consistency without matching feedback.
- **Related:** `ARC-011` (parallel subsystems) is structural; this Finding is interaction-only.

---

### UX-004 — Create-new company acknowledgment exists only on Partner Alumni imports

- **Why it matters:** Creating many new companies during import is high-cost and hard to undo (discard keeps companies — stated in discard copy). Partner Alumni requires an explicit create-new acknowledgment modal (count + checkbox + audit) before materialize; sponsor and exhibitor **Import to draft** proceed without that gate. Operators doing the same irreversible catalog create get unequal error prevention across importers.
- **Severity:** High · **Effort:** Medium
- **Evidence:**
  - `partner-alumni-import/.../ReviewQueueStep.tsx` + `CreateNewAcknowledgmentModal.tsx` — blocks when `pendingCreateNewCount > 0` until acknowledged
  - `partner-alumni-import` server — `create_new_acknowledged_*` fields enforced in materialize pipeline
  - `sponsor-import/.../ReviewQueueStep.tsx` and `exhibitor-import/.../ReviewQueueStep.tsx` — sticky **Import to draft →** with no create-new acknowledgment
  - `DiscardImportModal` (sponsor) notes companies created during import are kept
- **Status:** Open
- **Recommended action:** Extend the PA create-new acknowledgment pattern to sponsor and exhibitor import-to-draft (or an equivalent count + explicit confirm), so all importers gate irreversible company creation consistently.
- **Scope:** Sponsor, exhibitor, and Partner Alumni import review → draft materialization.
- **Validation / acceptance criteria:** Any import path that will create N>0 new companies requires an explicit, counted acknowledgment before materialize; audit trail parity where already present for PA.
- **Uncertainty / false-positive risk:** Medium — sponsor/exhibitor may rely on later draft review of **links**; that does not replace a create-count gate for company rows that survive discard. Not a clone of `ARC-011` (structure); interaction/error-prevention only.
- **Related:** `ARC-011`; `PROD-003` (Dashboard resume) is separate.

## Observations (not tracked)

### Strengths

- Company merge: impact preview + type `MERGE` confirm (`MergeConfirmDialog`).
- Remove sponsor/exhibitor/organizer modals clarify link vs company deletion; public rank-1 sponsor warnings where applicable.
- Import discard modals and shared stepper/progress/error banners across importers.
- Event Explorer fetch errors: keep previous rows, revert toward last success, Retry + `role="alert"`.
- Mobile filter drawer: focus trap, Escape, restore focus.
- Public edition tabs: shareable `?tab=`, labeled tablist, Overview deep-links.
- Login: labeled fields, busy states, safe redirect handling.
- Partner Alumni create-new acknowledgment is a strong pattern (`UX-004` asks to spread it).

### Report-only notes

- **Publish enabled when draft summary fails** (`PublishStep` sponsor/exhibitor): error banner shown but Publish still enabled when `diff` is null — meaningful residual; under-tracked relative to `UX-004` this cycle; revisit if publish mistakes recur.
- **Edition “Imports” tab is sponsor-only; exhibitor imports nested as Exhibitors → Bulk Upload** — wayfinding friction among existing controls; under-track vs opening a fifth Finding; related to `ARC-011` placement.
- **Sponsor directory fetch errors** do not revert params / lack Retry (Events does better) — report-only Medium residual.
- **EventGrid** replaces results with skeleton while pending (Sponsors dim prior rows) — interaction cost; under-track beside `UX-001`/`002`.
- **Nested `<label>` in Event filter checkbox groups** (`FilterField` + inner labels) — a11y smell; under-track without separate WCAG Finding this cycle.
- **Admin drawers/modals** often lack Escape/focus trap (`AdminDrawerShell`) — practical a11y residual; under-track.
- **Rejected without Finding:** dark mode, skeletons-as-taste, toast library, command palette, card redesigns, visual polish without task harm.

### Limitations

- Static code + pattern comparison; no authenticated end-to-end click-through of every wizard step.
- No analytics / session recordings.
- Cadence is Quarterly; cycle token `2026-07` as requested.
